news.title: Binance Secures Recovery Order, but Frozen Assets Do Not Establish Customer Repayment
news.body: Binance obtained an Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts order to support recovery after the October 29 attack. PYMNTS reports $6.3 billion stolen and more than $2.7 billion frozen through public- and private-sector efforts; freezing does not establish customer repayment. The publication separately reports a $6.5 billion freezing order—not assets located or recovered, or a revised loss estimate—but does not establish its full scope or explain the $200 million difference from the reported theft. Withdrawals had reopened on 87 networks as of November 14. As of November 19, the supplied reporting does not confirm whether Binance met its target to restore the remaining networks this week.

news.title: Supreme Court Declines Custodia Appeal, Leaving Fed Master-Account Discretion Intact
news.body: The Supreme Court declined to hear Custodia Bank’s master-account petition, leaving lower-court rulings intact rather than issuing a merits decision barring crypto-focused institutions from Fed access. Custodia remains without direct settlement access and dependent on intermediary banks. Limited-function “skinny” accounts represent a separate potential route, but the report identifies no new Custodia application or approval for one.

news.title: Klarna Expands Longer-Term Financing to 283,000 Merchants and Invites Users to AI Concierge
news.body: Approximately 283,000 merchants now offer Klarna’s longer-term financing, up from about 150,000 a year earlier. Separately, Klarna began inviting users to an AI shopping assistant that supports Klarna payment methods or a user’s debit card; a spokesperson said it cannot complete purchases without human payment authorization. Third-quarter revenue rose 12% to $1 billion while the net loss narrowed to $65 million. Klarna’s 3%–4% transaction-margin target for longer-term financing remains a target, not a reported portfolio result.

news.title: OneMain Wins Bank Approvals With $341 Million Initial-Capital Requirement
news.body: FDIC and Utah regulators approved OneMain’s proposed industrial bank, with launch anticipated in approximately one year. Before opening, OneMain must satisfy conditions including at least $341 million in initial capital and a 15% minimum leverage ratio. The planned bank would support deposit-funded personal loans, auto finance and credit cards. It is not yet operating, and OneMain has not disclosed realized funding savings from the structure.

news.title: Chargebee Adds Human-Reviewed AI Workflows for Contracts, Receivables and Revenue Recognition
news.body: Chargebee launched Arc agents for contract ingestion, receivables and revenue recognition, alongside an Agent Studio for custom workflows. According to the company announcement reported by PYMNTS, the described agent actions include citations and logs and remain subject to review before commitment. That description establishes approval controls for those workflows, not a product-wide prohibition on autonomous collections or payment execution. Chargebee provided no measured collection or productivity gains.

perspective: OneMain’s conditional bank approvals and Chargebee’s reviewed billing workflows anchor today’s thread on funding access and financial automation.
